description: FRONT DOOR — SCENE ROUTER: the scene-first way to generate es-plus code. Call with `scene` = what the user is building ('crud' page / standalone 'table' / standalone 'form' / 'dialog') and `intent` = that scene's intent table. For scene='crud' the intent is exactly the generate_crud argument object (name, apiUrl, surfaces — your one reasoning step is still filling `surfaces`); for the fragment scenes it is exactly the generate_table / generate_form / generate_dialog argument object. Routing and emission are deterministic, and the output is byte-identical to the corresponding legacy tool. When the client supports MCP structured output, the artifact envelope (`contract` / `files` / `config` / `warnings` / `fingerprint`) is also returned as `structuredContent`; the text content is unchanged. Use generate_composition when several of these pieces must live TOGETHER in one page; `generate_crud` remains available as the compatibility entry for a plain list/table page and produces the same bytes as scene='crud'.

intent.description: The scene's intent table. scene='crud': the page intent (name/apiUrl/surfaces/…). scene='table'|'form'|'dialog': that standalone artifact's intent (fields/…). Fill only the keys for the chosen scene; unknown keys are rejected with a did-you-mean.

scene.description: Which artifact the user wants: 'crud' (a full page with a table — the composite case), 'table' (one standalone es-table), 'form' (one standalone es-form), 'dialog' (one reusable add/edit dialog). Pick by WHAT is being built, not by which tool name you remember.

name: generate_scene

contract.description: Envelope protocol version: es-plus.artifact@2 or es-plus.composition@3

fingerprint.description: Content fingerprint of the artifact / composition
